harvestMonths.region: South African botanical account — approximate ripe figs
harvestMonths.notes: The source distinguishes September production from December ripeness. It does not establish all September–March months as ripe harvest.

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: No qualified numeric planting-to-first-food age in the checked sources. Record planting date, starting age and actual bearing.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: No measured full-bearing age was established; no yield ramp is inferred.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: No qualified food kg per plant with age, edible-product basis and management context. Missing output is unknown.

chillUnits.notes: No cultivar-specific numeric chilling requirement verified.

pollination.notes: No source-supported universal pollen classification established.

supplementaryReferences.title: Edible part and local use
supplementaryReferences.note: These are the source's signs for figs eaten by local people. Broad September–March fig production is not the same as ripe picking.

care: This large tree requires substantial space away from buildings, paving, sewer lines and walls because SANBI reports aggressive roots.
The source limits it to frost-free areas with moderate rainfall.
purchase: Confirm Ficus sur and the space available before buying. No numeric bearing age or household kg was verified.

sourceChecks.observations: Read indexed primary SANBI page content. Direct PlantZAfrica requests in this audit returned HTTP 403; this is not a claim that every individual endpoint was live-tested.

gaps: December is an approximate botanical ripe reference, not a guaranteed local first/last-pick interval.
